input: How long do I normally have to request a return?
ground_truth: The ordinary return request period is 30 days from delivery. Explain that this is the standard window without making claims about a particular order.
actual_output: You have 30 calendar days from the day your item is delivered to submit a return request. A request made on the 30th day is still within the normal window. If you submit a request after those 30 days, it will be reviewed manually to see if an exception can be made.

clauses.title: Goods received by the customer
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.1 Goods received by the customer
A customer may submit a return request within thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of the affected goods. The delivery date is day zero, and a request submitted on the thirtieth day is within the ordinary request period. The period runs from actual delivery, not the order date, payment date or dispatch date. Where an order is delivered in separate parcels, each affected item's period runs from delivery of the parcel containing that item. Delivery of another parcel from the same order does not shorten the period. If an item's delivery date or parcel allocation cannot be established, the request will require clarification or human review. The date the request was first recorded determines whether it was submitted on time. A timely request does not become late because inspection or review takes place later. However, timely submission does not waive the conditions relating to evidence, item condition or return shipment. For example, goods delivered on 5 October have an ordinary request deadline of 4 November, inclusive. Requests outside the ordinary return period are addressed in section 2.6.

clauses.title: Requests outside the ordinary conditions
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.6 Requests outside the ordinary conditions
A request submitted after thirty days will be referred for human review of the stated circumstances. It is not automatically accepted or rejected. Any approved exception must identify the goods and the condition or deadline being varied. Contact with customer service or an unanswered earlier message does not, by itself, establish an approved extension. Digital goods, services and standalone promotional gifts are outside the standard physical-return process. A claim concerning such a purchase requires human review; absence of a physical-return process does not automatically determine whether a separate refund claim is valid.

clauses.section_title: Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
clauses.title: Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.5 Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
Goods marked final sale at the time of purchase are excluded from change-of-mind returns. A product's general category or a label added after purchase does not establish that it was sold as final sale. Notwithstanding that exclusion, a request concerning verified arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item may be accepted within the period in section 2.1. In those circumstances, the unused and original-packaging conditions may be waived where opening, testing or loss of packaging was reasonably connected with discovering or reporting the fault. Secure return packaging is still required where the goods are to be returned. This exception does not cover damage caused by later misuse, extend the thirty-day request period or establish an entitlement to a refund without assessment. Evidence and any required inspection remain applicable. Missing original packaging alone is not a sufficient reason to reject a qualifying damaged-item claim.

clauses.title: Refund timeframe
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.4 Refund timeframe
The store targets refund initiation within two (2) business days after final acceptance and completion of the required receipt and inspection, or an approved waiver. Return authorization alone does not start this period. After processing, supported card and PayNow refunds normally appear within five (5) to ten (10) business days. These are estimated periods rather than guaranteed posting dates. Requested, accepted and pending refunds may not yet have been processed.

name: returns-and-refunds
description: Policy guidance for return eligibility and refund handling.
---
# Returns and refunds

Read the matching clause before recommending or requesting an action. The deterministic rule engine is authoritative for refund approval limits.

- `eligibility.md`: Sections 1–2. Return eligibility, request windows, qualifying reasons and change-of-mind conditions.
- `evidence.md`: Section 3. Required, unavailable, inaccessible or unsafe evidence.
- `return-procedure.md`: Section 4. Return authorization, dispatch, arrangements, packaging and unsafe returns.
- `shipping-fees.md`: Section 5. Return-shipping and outbound-shipping costs.
- `disputes.md`: Section 7. Return-parcel disputes, inspection disagreements and counterfeit claims.
- `refunds.md`: Contains section 6. Includes refund methods, timing and approval limits.

<!-- Generated from data/policy/pdf; run scripts/sync_skills.py to refresh. -->

## RET-Application-1 Application for returns and refunds

Subject to the conditions in this Policy, customers may apply for the return of purchased goods and/or a refund. A request may concern goods received by the customer or goods that have not been received. Submission of a request does not, by itself, constitute acceptance of the return or approval of a refund. This Policy applies to physical goods purchased in Singapore dollars for delivery within Singapore. The same standard conditions apply to all customer loyalty tiers. All dates are assessed in Singapore time. Calendar days include weekends and public holidays. Where a period is stated in business days, Saturdays, Sundays and Singapore public holidays are excluded. A specific exception changes only the condition expressly identified; the remaining conditions continue to apply.

## 2. Application for the return of goods

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.1 Goods received by the customer

A customer may submit a return request within thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of the affected goods. The delivery date is day zero, and a request submitted on the thirtieth day is within the ordinary request period. The period runs from actual delivery, not the order date, payment date or dispatch date. Where an order is delivered in separate parcels, each affected item's period runs from delivery of the parcel containing that item. Delivery of another parcel from the same order does not shorten the period. If an item's delivery date or parcel allocation cannot be established, the request will require clarification or human review. The date the request was first recorded determines whether it was submitted on time. A timely request does not become late because inspection or review takes place later. However, timely submission does not waive the conditions relating to evidence, item condition or return shipment. For example, goods delivered on 5 October have an ordinary request deadline of 4 November, inclusive. Requests outside the ordinary return period are addressed in section 2.6.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnEligibility-2.6.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.2 Goods not received by the customer

A customer may raise a non-receipt claim where: (i) the estimated delivery date has passed and the parcel has not arrived; (ii) tracking shows delivery but the customer has not received the parcel; or (iii) the carrier has confirmed that the parcel was lost or damaged in transit. ## RET-Application-1 Application for returns and refunds

Subject to the conditions in this Policy, customers may apply for the return of purchased goods and/or a refund. A request may concern goods received by the customer or goods that have not been received. Submission of a request does not, by itself, constitute acceptance of the return or approval of a refund. This Policy applies to physical goods purchased in Singapore dollars for delivery within Singapore. The same standard conditions apply to all customer loyalty tiers. All dates are assessed in Singapore time. Calendar days include weekends and public holidays. Where a period is stated in business days, Saturdays, Sundays and Singapore public holidays are excluded. A specific exception changes only the condition expressly identified; the remaining conditions continue to apply.

## 2. Application for the return of goods

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.1 Goods received by the customer

A customer may submit a return request within thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of the affected goods. The delivery date is day zero, and a request submitted on the thirtieth day is within the ordinary request period. The period runs from actual delivery, not the order date, payment date or dispatch date. Where an order is delivered in separate parcels, each affected item's period runs from delivery of the parcel containing that item. Delivery of another parcel from the same order does not shorten the period. If an item's delivery date or parcel allocation cannot be established, the request will require clarification or human review. The date the request was first recorded determines whether it was submitted on time. A timely request does not become late because inspection or review takes place later. However, timely submission does not waive the conditions relating to evidence, item condition or return shipment. For example, goods delivered on 5 October have an ordinary request deadline of 4 November, inclusive. Requests outside the ordinary return period are addressed in section 2.6.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnEligibility-2.6.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.2 Goods not received by the customer

A customer may raise a non-receipt claim where: (i) the estimated delivery date has passed and the parcel has not arrived; (ii) tracking shows delivery but the customer has not received the parcel; or (iii) the carrier has confirmed that the parcel was lost or damaged in transit. Non-receipt claims require investigation of the shipment status, delivery records and any carrier findings. A non-receipt claim does not require the customer to return goods that they do not possess. A refund remains subject to the investigation outcome and the conditions in section 6 of this Policy.

Related clauses: REF-Refunds-6.1, REF-Refunds-6.2, REF-Refunds-6.3, REF-Refunds-6.4, REF-Refunds-6.5, REF-Refunds-6.6.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.3 Reasons for a return request

A return and/or refund may be requested in the following circumstances: (a) the parcel is empty or the quantity received is less than the quantity purchased; (b) supplied accessories or components are missing; (c) the goods differ from the purchased item or variant, such as a different model, size or colour; (d) the goods are defective or do not function as intended; (e) the goods sustained physical damage before or during delivery; or (f) the customer wishes to return goods in their original, unused condition due to a change of mind. The reason selected must correspond to the issue reported. A concern that goods may be counterfeit is subject to human review under section 7.3 rather than an automatic refund or rejection. Before goods are treated as missing, any outstanding parcels from the same order must be taken into account.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnParcelDisputes-7.3.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.4 Change-of-mind returns

A change-of-mind return is available within the period in section 2.1 only where the goods: (i) are unused and in their original condition; (ii) remain in their original packaging; (iii) retain original tags or labels, where supplied; (iv) include all accessories, components and gifts supplied with the purchase; and (v) were not designated final sale at the time of purchase. The affected goods and quantities must be identified in the request. Goods returned as part of an approved bundle must include the components specified in that return authorization. A change in preference is not treated as a defect where the goods match the purchased specification. The conditions for damaged, faulty or incorrect goods, including exceptions to final-sale and original-packaging requirements, are set out in section 2.5.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnEligibility-2.1, RET-ReturnEligibility-2.5.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.5 Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception

Goods marked final sale at the time of purchase are excluded from change-of-mind returns. A product's general category or a label added after purchase does not establish that it was sold as final sale. Notwithstanding that exclusion, a request concerning verified arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item may be accepted within the period in section 2.1. In those circumstances, the unused and original-packaging conditions may be waived where opening, testing or loss of packaging was reasonably connected with discovering or reporting the fault. Secure return packaging is still required where the goods are to be returned. This exception does not cover damage caused by later misuse, extend the thirty-day request period or establish an entitlement to a refund without assessment. Evidence and any required inspection remain applicable. Missing original packaging alone is not a sufficient reason to reject a qualifying damaged-item claim.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnEligibility-2.1.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.6 Requests outside the ordinary conditions

A request submitted after thirty days will be referred for human review of the stated circumstances. It is not automatically accepted or rejected. Any approved exception must identify the goods and the condition or deadline being varied. Contact with customer service or an unanswered earlier message does not, by itself, establish an approved extension. Digital goods, services and standalone promotional gifts are outside the standard physical-return process. A claim concerning such a purchase requires human review; absence of a physical-return process does not automatically determine whether a separate refund claim is valid.

Subject to the conditions in this Policy, customers may apply for the return of purchased goods and/or a refund. A customer may submit a return request within thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of the affected goods. clauses.title: Goods received by the customer
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.1 Goods received by the customer
A customer may submit a return request within thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of the affected goods. The delivery date is day zero, and a request submitted on the thirtieth day is within the ordinary request period. The period runs from actual delivery, not the order date, payment date or dispatch date. Where an order is delivered in separate parcels, each affected item's period runs from delivery of the parcel containing that item. Delivery of another parcel from the same order does not shorten the period. If an item's delivery date or parcel allocation cannot be established, the request will require clarification or human review. The date the request was first recorded determines whether it was submitted on time. A timely request does not become late because inspection or review takes place later. However, timely submission does not waive the conditions relating to evidence, item condition or return shipment. For example, goods delivered on 5 October have an ordinary request deadline of 4 November, inclusive. Requests outside the ordinary return period are addressed in section 2.6.

clauses.title: Requests outside the ordinary conditions
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.6 Requests outside the ordinary conditions
A request submitted after thirty days will be referred for human review of the stated circumstances. It is not automatically accepted or rejected. Any approved exception must identify the goods and the condition or deadline being varied. Contact with customer service or an unanswered earlier message does not, by itself, establish an approved extension. Digital goods, services and standalone promotional gifts are outside the standard physical-return process. A claim concerning such a purchase requires human review; absence of a physical-return process does not automatically determine whether a separate refund claim is valid.

clauses.title: Refund timeframe
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.4 Refund timeframe
The store targets refund initiation within two (2) business days after final acceptance and completion of the required receipt and inspection, or an approved waiver. Return authorization alone does not start this period. After processing, supported card and PayNow refunds normally appear within five (5) to ten (10) business days. These are estimated periods rather than guaranteed posting dates. Requested, accepted and pending refunds may not yet have been processed.

clauses.title: Conditions for payment
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.1 Conditions for payment
A refund is issued after the request has been accepted and, where a physical return is required, the returned goods have been received and the applicable inspection completed. The inspection considers the identity, quantities, completeness and conditions relevant to the original return reason, including any exception in section 2.5. The store targets inspection within three (3) business days after warehouse receipt. Return tracking marked delivered does not itself establish that inspection is complete. A delay or a disputed finding may be raised for review under section 7. A return recorded as requested or received may still be progressing through the ordinary return process. That status alone does not require human review or establish that a refund is due. Routine progress enquiries may be answered automatically using the confirmed records. A disputed finding, unavailable required evidence or a request for human assistance must be referred for human review. Physical return may be waived following human review where non-delivery is confirmed or return is unsafe or impractical. The waiver applies only to the goods and resolution specified. It does not remove the requirement to establish the payment and refundable amount.

clauses.section_title: Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
clauses.title: Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.5 Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
Goods marked final sale at the time of purchase are excluded from change-of-mind returns. A product's general category or a label added after purchase does not establish that it was sold as final sale. Notwithstanding that exclusion, a request concerning verified arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item may be accepted within the period in section 2.1. In those circumstances, the unused and original-packaging conditions may be waived where opening, testing or loss of packaging was reasonably connected with discovering or reporting the fault. Secure return packaging is still required where the goods are to be returned. This exception does not cover damage caused by later misuse, extend the thirty-day request period or establish an entitlement to a refund without assessment. Evidence and any required inspection remain applicable. Missing original packaging alone is not a sufficient reason to reject a qualifying damaged-item claim.

clauses.title: Grounds for a dispute
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.1 Grounds for a dispute
A dispute may be raised concerning: (a) a return parcel reported as not received; (b) missing goods, quantities, accessories or bundle components; (c) a different item in the returned parcel; (d) damage, a fault or a condition inconsistent with the accepted return reason; (e) the authenticity of purchased or returned goods; or (f) whether a change-of-mind return meets the applicable condition requirements. A dispute initiates a review. It does not establish that either party's account is correct or create a second refund entitlement.

clauses.section_title: Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
clauses.title: Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.2 Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
The original return reason, purchase details, supporting evidence and inspection findings will be considered together. Review must distinguish the original reported fault from an allegation of additional damage, missing contents or a different item during the return. The customer is not automatically responsible for damage merely because the goods were returned damaged. A qualifying original fault remains subject to section 2.5. Conflicting accounts or inspection findings will be referred for human review rather than automatic refund or rejection.

clauses.title: Counterfeit products
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.3 Counterfeit products
A claim concerning authenticity will be referred for human review. Relevant product, packaging and purchase evidence may be requested. A brand name, low price, image or allegation alone does not establish that goods are genuine or counterfeit. Any accepted resolution will identify the affected goods, whether physical return is required and the applicable refund. No special compensation or determination of authenticity is implied merely by raising the claim.

clauses.section_title: Goods returned due to change of mind
clauses.title: Goods returned due to change of mind
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.4 Goods returned due to change of mind
A dispute may arise where inspection reports use, missing original packaging or tags, missing accessories, an incomplete bundle or a different item. The applicable conditions are those in section 2.4 and the agreed return authorization. If the customer contests the finding, the request will be referred for human review. Where the original reason concerns arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item, section 2.5 must be considered rather than applying change-of-mind conditions without that exception.

clauses.title: Review and communication
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.5 Review and communication
The store may request further relevant evidence and will communicate the reviewed outcome and its reason. An unresolved allegation is not proof of misuse, fraud or ineligibility. Unavailable or unsafe evidence is handled under section 3.2. A customer may request human review of a disputed decision. Existing case details and additional evidence should remain associated with the same request. Contact with support is not, by itself, confirmation that an investigation, amendment or payment has been completed.

clauses.title: Goods received by the customer
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.1 Goods received by the customer
A customer may submit a return request within thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of the affected goods. The delivery date is day zero, and a request submitted on the thirtieth day is within the ordinary request period. The period runs from actual delivery, not the order date, payment date or dispatch date. Where an order is delivered in separate parcels, each affected item's period runs from delivery of the parcel containing that item. Delivery of another parcel from the same order does not shorten the period. If an item's delivery date or parcel allocation cannot be established, the request will require clarification or human review. The date the request was first recorded determines whether it was submitted on time. A timely request does not become late because inspection or review takes place later. However, timely submission does not waive the conditions relating to evidence, item condition or return shipment. For example, goods delivered on 5 October have an ordinary request deadline of 4 November, inclusive. Requests outside the ordinary return period are addressed in section 2.6.

clauses.title: Reasons for a return request
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.3 Reasons for a return request
A return and/or refund may be requested in the following circumstances: (a) the parcel is empty or the quantity received is less than the quantity purchased; (b) supplied accessories or components are missing; (c) the goods differ from the purchased item or variant, such as a different model, size or colour; (d) the goods are defective or do not function as intended; (e) the goods sustained physical damage before or during delivery; or (f) the customer wishes to return goods in their original, unused condition due to a change of mind. The reason selected must correspond to the issue reported. A concern that goods may be counterfeit is subject to human review under section 7.3 rather than an automatic refund or rejection. Before goods are treated as missing, any outstanding parcels from the same order must be taken into account.

clauses.title: Conditions for payment
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.1 Conditions for payment
A refund is issued after the request has been accepted and, where a physical return is required, the returned goods have been received and the applicable inspection completed. The inspection considers the identity, quantities, completeness and conditions relevant to the original return reason, including any exception in section 2.5. The store targets inspection within three (3) business days after warehouse receipt. Return tracking marked delivered does not itself establish that inspection is complete. A delay or a disputed finding may be raised for review under section 7. A return recorded as requested or received may still be progressing through the ordinary return process. That status alone does not require human review or establish that a refund is due. Routine progress enquiries may be answered automatically using the confirmed records. A disputed finding, unavailable required evidence or a request for human assistance must be referred for human review. Physical return may be waived following human review where non-delivery is confirmed or return is unsafe or impractical. The waiver applies only to the goods and resolution specified. It does not remove the requirement to establish the payment and refundable amount.

clauses.title: Requests outside the ordinary conditions
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.6 Requests outside the ordinary conditions
A request submitted after thirty days will be referred for human review of the stated circumstances. It is not automatically accepted or rejected. Any approved exception must identify the goods and the condition or deadline being varied. Contact with customer service or an unanswered earlier message does not, by itself, establish an approved extension. Digital goods, services and standalone promotional gifts are outside the standard physical-return process. A claim concerning such a purchase requires human review; absence of a physical-return process does not automatically determine whether a separate refund claim is valid.

clauses.title: Counterfeit products
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.3 Counterfeit products
A claim concerning authenticity will be referred for human review. Relevant product, packaging and purchase evidence may be requested. A brand name, low price, image or allegation alone does not establish that goods are genuine or counterfeit. Any accepted resolution will identify the affected goods, whether physical return is required and the applicable refund. No special compensation or determination of authenticity is implied merely by raising the claim.

clauses.section_title: Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
clauses.title: Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.5 Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
Goods marked final sale at the time of purchase are excluded from change-of-mind returns. A product's general category or a label added after purchase does not establish that it was sold as final sale. Notwithstanding that exclusion, a request concerning verified arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item may be accepted within the period in section 2.1. In those circumstances, the unused and original-packaging conditions may be waived where opening, testing or loss of packaging was reasonably connected with discovering or reporting the fault. Secure return packaging is still required where the goods are to be returned. This exception does not cover damage caused by later misuse, extend the thirty-day request period or establish an entitlement to a refund without assessment. Evidence and any required inspection remain applicable. Missing original packaging alone is not a sufficient reason to reject a qualifying damaged-item claim.

clauses.title: Grounds for a dispute
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.1 Grounds for a dispute
A dispute may be raised concerning: (a) a return parcel reported as not received; (b) missing goods, quantities, accessories or bundle components; (c) a different item in the returned parcel; (d) damage, a fault or a condition inconsistent with the accepted return reason; (e) the authenticity of purchased or returned goods; or (f) whether a change-of-mind return meets the applicable condition requirements. A dispute initiates a review. It does not establish that either party's account is correct or create a second refund entitlement.

clauses.section_title: Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
clauses.title: Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.2 Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
The original return reason, purchase details, supporting evidence and inspection findings will be considered together. Review must distinguish the original reported fault from an allegation of additional damage, missing contents or a different item during the return. The customer is not automatically responsible for damage merely because the goods were returned damaged. A qualifying original fault remains subject to section 2.5. Conflicting accounts or inspection findings will be referred for human review rather than automatic refund or rejection.

clauses.section_title: Goods returned due to change of mind
clauses.title: Goods returned due to change of mind
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.4 Goods returned due to change of mind
A dispute may arise where inspection reports use, missing original packaging or tags, missing accessories, an incomplete bundle or a different item. The applicable conditions are those in section 2.4 and the agreed return authorization. If the customer contests the finding, the request will be referred for human review. Where the original reason concerns arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item, section 2.5 must be considered rather than applying change-of-mind conditions without that exception.

clauses.title: Review and communication
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.5 Review and communication
The store may request further relevant evidence and will communicate the reviewed outcome and its reason. An unresolved allegation is not proof of misuse, fraud or ineligibility. Unavailable or unsafe evidence is handled under section 3.2. A customer may request human review of a disputed decision. Existing case details and additional evidence should remain associated with the same request. Contact with support is not, by itself, confirmation that an investigation, amendment or payment has been completed.

## RET-Application-1 Application for returns and refunds

Subject to the conditions in this Policy, customers may apply for the return of purchased goods and/or a refund. A request may concern goods received by the customer or goods that have not been received. Submission of a request does not, by itself, constitute acceptance of the return or approval of a refund. This Policy applies to physical goods purchased in Singapore dollars for delivery within Singapore. The same standard conditions apply to all customer loyalty tiers. All dates are assessed in Singapore time. Calendar days include weekends and public holidays. Where a period is stated in business days, Saturdays, Sundays and Singapore public holidays are excluded. A specific exception changes only the condition expressly identified; the remaining conditions continue to apply.

## 2. Application for the return of goods

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.1 Goods received by the customer

A customer may submit a return request within thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of the affected goods. The delivery date is day zero, and a request submitted on the thirtieth day is within the ordinary request period. The period runs from actual delivery, not the order date, payment date or dispatch date. Where an order is delivered in separate parcels, each affected item's period runs from delivery of the parcel containing that item. Delivery of another parcel from the same order does not shorten the period. If an item's delivery date or parcel allocation cannot be established, the request will require clarification or human review. The date the request was first recorded determines whether it was submitted on time. A timely request does not become late because inspection or review takes place later. However, timely submission does not waive the conditions relating to evidence, item condition or return shipment. For example, goods delivered on 5 October have an ordinary request deadline of 4 November, inclusive. Requests outside the ordinary return period are addressed in section 2.6.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnEligibility-2.6.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.2 Goods not received by the customer

A customer may raise a non-receipt claim where: (i) the estimated delivery date has passed and the parcel has not arrived; (ii) tracking shows delivery but the customer has not received the parcel; or (iii) the carrier has confirmed that the parcel was lost or damaged in transit. Non-receipt claims require investigation of the shipment status, delivery records and any carrier findings. A non-receipt claim does not require the customer to return goods that they do not possess. A refund remains subject to the investigation outcome and the conditions in section 6 of this Policy.

Related clauses: REF-Refunds-6.1, REF-Refunds-6.2, REF-Refunds-6.3, REF-Refunds-6.4, REF-Refunds-6.5, REF-Refunds-6.6.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.3 Reasons for a return request

A return and/or refund may be requested in the following circumstances: (a) the parcel is empty or the quantity received is less than the quantity purchased; (b) supplied accessories or components are missing; (c) the goods differ from the purchased item or variant, such as a different model, size or colour; (d) the goods are defective or do not function as intended; (e) the goods sustained physical damage before or during delivery; or (f) the customer wishes to return goods in their original, unused condition due to a change of mind. The reason selected must correspond to the issue reported. A concern that goods may be counterfeit is subject to human review under section 7.3 rather than an automatic refund or rejection. Before goods are treated as missing, any outstanding parcels from the same order must be taken into account.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnParcelDisputes-7.3.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.4 Change-of-mind returns

A change-of-mind return is available within the period in section 2.1 only where the goods: (i) are unused and in their original condition; (ii) remain in their original packaging; (iii) retain original tags or labels, where supplied; (iv) include all accessories, components and gifts supplied with the purchase; and (v) were not designated final sale at the time of purchase. The affected goods and quantities must be identified in the request. Goods returned as part of an approved bundle must include the components specified in that return authorization. A change in preference is not treated as a defect where the goods match the purchased specification. The conditions for damaged, faulty or incorrect goods, including exceptions to final-sale and original-packaging requirements, are set out in section 2.5.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnEligibility-2.1, RET-ReturnEligibility-2.5.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.5 Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception

clauses.title: Goods received by the customer
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.1 Goods received by the customer
A customer may submit a return request within thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of the affected goods. The delivery date is day zero, and a request submitted on the thirtieth day is within the ordinary request period. The period runs from actual delivery, not the order date, payment date or dispatch date. Where an order is delivered in separate parcels, each affected item's period runs from delivery of the parcel containing that item. Delivery of another parcel from the same order does not shorten the period. If an item's delivery date or parcel allocation cannot be established, the request will require clarification or human review. The date the request was first recorded determines whether it was submitted on time. A timely request does not become late because inspection or review takes place later. However, timely submission does not waive the conditions relating to evidence, item condition or return shipment. For example, goods delivered on 5 October have an ordinary request deadline of 4 November, inclusive. Requests outside the ordinary return period are addressed in section 2.6.

clauses.title: Requests outside the ordinary conditions
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.6 Requests outside the ordinary conditions
A request submitted after thirty days will be referred for human review of the stated circumstances. It is not automatically accepted or rejected. Any approved exception must identify the goods and the condition or deadline being varied. Contact with customer service or an unanswered earlier message does not, by itself, establish an approved extension. Digital goods, services and standalone promotional gifts are outside the standard physical-return process. A claim concerning such a purchase requires human review; absence of a physical-return process does not automatically determine whether a separate refund claim is valid.

clauses.title: Refund timeframe
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.4 Refund timeframe
The store targets refund initiation within two (2) business days after final acceptance and completion of the required receipt and inspection, or an approved waiver. Return authorization alone does not start this period. After processing, supported card and PayNow refunds normally appear within five (5) to ten (10) business days. These are estimated periods rather than guaranteed posting dates. Requested, accepted and pending refunds may not yet have been processed.

clauses.section_title: Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
clauses.title: Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.5 Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
Goods marked final sale at the time of purchase are excluded from change-of-mind returns. A product's general category or a label added after purchase does not establish that it was sold as final sale. Notwithstanding that exclusion, a request concerning verified arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item may be accepted within the period in section 2.1. In those circumstances, the unused and original-packaging conditions may be waived where opening, testing or loss of packaging was reasonably connected with discovering or reporting the fault. Secure return packaging is still required where the goods are to be returned. This exception does not cover damage caused by later misuse, extend the thirty-day request period or establish an entitlement to a refund without assessment. Evidence and any required inspection remain applicable. Missing original packaging alone is not a sufficient reason to reject a qualifying damaged-item claim.

clauses.title: Conditions for payment
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.1 Conditions for payment
A refund is issued after the request has been accepted and, where a physical return is required, the returned goods have been received and the applicable inspection completed. The inspection considers the identity, quantities, completeness and conditions relevant to the original return reason, including any exception in section 2.5. The store targets inspection within three (3) business days after warehouse receipt. Return tracking marked delivered does not itself establish that inspection is complete. A delay or a disputed finding may be raised for review under section 7. A return recorded as requested or received may still be progressing through the ordinary return process. That status alone does not require human review or establish that a refund is due. Routine progress enquiries may be answered automatically using the confirmed records. A disputed finding, unavailable required evidence or a request for human assistance must be referred for human review. Physical return may be waived following human review where non-delivery is confirmed or return is unsafe or impractical. The waiver applies only to the goods and resolution specified. It does not remove the requirement to establish the payment and refundable amount.

clauses.title: Grounds for a dispute
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.1 Grounds for a dispute
A dispute may be raised concerning: (a) a return parcel reported as not received; (b) missing goods, quantities, accessories or bundle components; (c) a different item in the returned parcel; (d) damage, a fault or a condition inconsistent with the accepted return reason; (e) the authenticity of purchased or returned goods; or (f) whether a change-of-mind return meets the applicable condition requirements. A dispute initiates a review. It does not establish that either party's account is correct or create a second refund entitlement.

clauses.section_title: Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
clauses.title: Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.2 Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
The original return reason, purchase details, supporting evidence and inspection findings will be considered together. Review must distinguish the original reported fault from an allegation of additional damage, missing contents or a different item during the return. The customer is not automatically responsible for damage merely because the goods were returned damaged. A qualifying original fault remains subject to section 2.5. Conflicting accounts or inspection findings will be referred for human review rather than automatic refund or rejection.

clauses.title: Counterfeit products
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.3 Counterfeit products
A claim concerning authenticity will be referred for human review. Relevant product, packaging and purchase evidence may be requested. A brand name, low price, image or allegation alone does not establish that goods are genuine or counterfeit. Any accepted resolution will identify the affected goods, whether physical return is required and the applicable refund. No special compensation or determination of authenticity is implied merely by raising the claim.

clauses.section_title: Goods returned due to change of mind
clauses.title: Goods returned due to change of mind
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.4 Goods returned due to change of mind
A dispute may arise where inspection reports use, missing original packaging or tags, missing accessories, an incomplete bundle or a different item. The applicable conditions are those in section 2.4 and the agreed return authorization. If the customer contests the finding, the request will be referred for human review. Where the original reason concerns arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item, section 2.5 must be considered rather than applying change-of-mind conditions without that exception.

clauses.title: Review and communication
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.5 Review and communication
The store may request further relevant evidence and will communicate the reviewed outcome and its reason. An unresolved allegation is not proof of misuse, fraud or ineligibility. Unavailable or unsafe evidence is handled under section 3.2. A customer may request human review of a disputed decision. Existing case details and additional evidence should remain associated with the same request. Contact with support is not, by itself, confirmation that an investigation, amendment or payment has been completed.

## RET-Application-1 Application for returns and refunds

Subject to the conditions in this Policy, customers may apply for the return of purchased goods and/or a refund. A request may concern goods received by the customer or goods that have not been received. Submission of a request does not, by itself, constitute acceptance of the return or approval of a refund. This Policy applies to physical goods purchased in Singapore dollars for delivery within Singapore. The same standard conditions apply to all customer loyalty tiers. All dates are assessed in Singapore time. Calendar days include weekends and public holidays. Where a period is stated in business days, Saturdays, Sundays and Singapore public holidays are excluded. A specific exception changes only the condition expressly identified; the remaining conditions continue to apply.

## 2. Application for the return of goods

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.1 Goods received by the customer

A customer may submit a return request within thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of the affected goods. The delivery date is day zero, and a request submitted on the thirtieth day is within the ordinary request period. The period runs from actual delivery, not the order date, payment date or dispatch date. Where an order is delivered in separate parcels, each affected item's period runs from delivery of the parcel containing that item. Delivery of another parcel from the same order does not shorten the period. If an item's delivery date or parcel allocation cannot be established, the request will require clarification or human review. The date the request was first recorded determines whether it was submitted on time. A timely request does not become late because inspection or review takes place later. However, timely submission does not waive the conditions relating to evidence, item condition or return shipment. For example, goods delivered on 5 October have an ordinary request deadline of 4 November, inclusive. Requests outside the ordinary return period are addressed in section 2.6.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnEligibility-2.6.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.2 Goods not received by the customer

A customer may raise a non-receipt claim where: (i) the estimated delivery date has passed and the parcel has not arrived; (ii) tracking shows delivery but the customer has not received the parcel; or (iii) the carrier has confirmed that the parcel was lost or damaged in transit. Non-receipt claims require investigation of the shipment status, delivery records and any carrier findings. A non-receipt claim does not require the customer to return goods that they do not possess. A refund remains subject to the investigation outcome and the conditions in section 6 of this Policy.

Related clauses: REF-Refunds-6.1, REF-Refunds-6.2, REF-Refunds-6.3, REF-Refunds-6.4, REF-Refunds-6.5, REF-Refunds-6.6.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.3 Reasons for a return request

A return and/or refund may be requested in the following circumstances: (a) the parcel is empty or the quantity received is less than the quantity purchased; (b) supplied accessories or components are missing; (c) the goods differ from the purchased item or variant, such as a different model, size or colour; (d) the goods are defective or do not function as intended; (e) the goods sustained physical damage before or during delivery; or (f) the customer wishes to return goods in their original, unused condition due to a change of mind. The reason selected must correspond to the issue reported. A concern that goods may be counterfeit is subject to human review under section 7.3 rather than an automatic refund or rejection. Before goods are treated as missing, any outstanding parcels from the same order must be taken into account.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnParcelDisputes-7.3.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.4 Change-of-mind returns

A change-of-mind return is available within the period in section 2.1 only where the goods: (i) are unused and in their original condition; (ii) remain in their original packaging; (iii) retain original tags or labels, where supplied; (iv) include all accessories, components and gifts supplied with the purchase; and (v) were not designated final sale at the time of purchase. The affected goods and quantities must be identified in the request. Goods returned as part of an approved bundle must include the components specified in that return authorization. A change in preference is not treated as a defect where the goods match the purchased specification. The conditions for damaged, faulty or incorrect goods, including exceptions to final-sale and original-packaging requirements, are set out in section 2.5.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnEligibility-2.1, RET-ReturnEligibility-2.5.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.5 Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception

Goods marked final sale at the time of purchase are excluded from change-of-mind returns. A product's general category or a label added after purchase does not establish that it was sold as final sale. Notwithstanding that exclusion, a request concerning verified arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item may be accepted within the period in section 2.1. In those circumstances, the unused and original-packaging conditions may be waived where opening, testing or loss of packaging was reasonably connected with discovering or reporting the fault. Secure return packaging is still required where the goods are to be returned. This exception does not cover damage caused by later misuse, extend the thirty-day request period or establish an entitlement to a refund without assessment. Evidence and any required inspection remain applicable. Missing original packaging alone is not a sufficient reason to reject a qualifying damaged-item claim.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnEligibility-2.1.

### RET-ReturnEligibility-2.6 Requests outside the ordinary conditions

A request submitted after thirty days will be referred for human review of the stated circumstances. It is not automatically accepted or rejected. Any approved exception must identify the goods and the condition or deadline being varied. Contact with customer service or an unanswered earlier message does not, by itself, establish an approved extension. Digital goods, services and standalone promotional gifts are outside the standard physical-return process. A claim concerning such a purchase requires human review; absence of a physical-return process does not automatically determine whether a separate refund claim is valid.

Subject to the conditions in this Policy, customers may apply for the return of purchased goods and/or a refund. This Policy applies to physical goods purchased in Singapore dollars for delivery within Singapore. The same standard conditions apply to all customer loyalty tiers. A customer may submit a return request within thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of the affected goods. The delivery date is day zero, and a request submitted on the thirtieth day is within the ordinary request period. The period runs from actual delivery, not the order date, payment date or dispatch date. Where an order is delivered in separate parcels, each affected item's period runs from delivery of the parcel containing that item. Delivery of another parcel from the same order does not shorten the period. If an item's delivery date or parcel allocation cannot be established, the request will require clarification or human review. The date the request was first recorded determines whether it was submitted on time. A timely request does not become late because inspection or review takes place later. For example, goods delivered on 5 October have an ordinary request deadline of 4 November, inclusive. Requests outside the ordinary return period are addressed in section 2.6.

A customer may raise a non-receipt claim where: (i) the estimated delivery date has passed and the parcel has not arrived; (ii) tracking shows delivery but the customer has not received the parcel; or (iii) the carrier has confirmed that the parcel was lost or damaged in transit. Non-receipt claims require investigation of the shipment status, delivery records and any carrier findings. A non-receipt claim does not require the customer to return goods that they do not possess. A return and/or refund may be requested in the following circumstances: (a) the parcel is empty or the quantity received is less than the quantity purchased; (b) supplied accessories or components are missing; (c) the goods differ from the purchased item or variant, such as a different model, size or colour; (d) the goods are defective or do not function as intended; (e) the goods sustained physical damage before or during delivery; or (f) the customer wishes to return goods in their original, unused condition due to a change of mind. clauses.title: Conditions for payment
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.1 Conditions for payment
A refund is issued after the request has been accepted and, where a physical return is required, the returned goods have been received and the applicable inspection completed. The inspection considers the identity, quantities, completeness and conditions relevant to the original return reason, including any exception in section 2.5. The store targets inspection within three (3) business days after warehouse receipt. Return tracking marked delivered does not itself establish that inspection is complete. A delay or a disputed finding may be raised for review under section 7. A return recorded as requested or received may still be progressing through the ordinary return process. That status alone does not require human review or establish that a refund is due. Routine progress enquiries may be answered automatically using the confirmed records. A disputed finding, unavailable required evidence or a request for human assistance must be referred for human review. Physical return may be waived following human review where non-delivery is confirmed or return is unsafe or impractical. The waiver applies only to the goods and resolution specified. It does not remove the requirement to establish the payment and refundable amount.

clauses.title: Refund approval requirements
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.6 Refund approval requirements
The approval requirements below apply only after the acceptance, inspection and payment conditions in sections 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 have been satisfied: (a) an eligible refund of SGD 30.00 or less may be processed automatically; (b) an eligible refund above SGD 30.00 and up to SGD 100.00 requires automated review before payment is approved; and (c) a refund above SGD 100.00 requires human review before payment is approved. Automated review must establish that the proposed action is supported by verified case facts, the applicable policy clauses and the approved refundable amount. A proposal that cannot be substantiated must be corrected or referred for human review; the amount alone does not establish eligibility. A requirement for human review elsewhere in this Policy takes precedence regardless of amount. In particular, disputed findings, unavailable or unsafe evidence and unapproved exceptions must not be resolved by automatic payment. An automatically issued return authorization does not establish that these payment requirements have been satisfied. The approval limits do not increase the captured balance available for refund, permit duplicate payment or allow a different payment destination.

clauses.title: Refund timeframe
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.4 Refund timeframe
The store targets refund initiation within two (2) business days after final acceptance and completion of the required receipt and inspection, or an approved waiver. Return authorization alone does not start this period. After processing, supported card and PayNow refunds normally appear within five (5) to ten (10) business days. These are estimated periods rather than guaranteed posting dates. Requested, accepted and pending refunds may not yet have been processed.

clauses.title: Payment destination and previous refunds
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.3 Payment destination and previous refunds
Refunds are made in SGD to the original payment method. They cannot be redirected to a different account or payment instrument supplied during a support conversation. The total of completed and pending refunds must not exceed the amount captured for the order. Amounts already refunded or reserved for an existing refund will be deducted from the remaining balance. Failed payments and uncaptured authorizations cannot be refunded as settled payments. Approval of a return does not authorize a duplicate refund.

clauses.section_title: Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
clauses.title: Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.5 Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
Goods marked final sale at the time of purchase are excluded from change-of-mind returns. A product's general category or a label added after purchase does not establish that it was sold as final sale. Notwithstanding that exclusion, a request concerning verified arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item may be accepted within the period in section 2.1. In those circumstances, the unused and original-packaging conditions may be waived where opening, testing or loss of packaging was reasonably connected with discovering or reporting the fault. Secure return packaging is still required where the goods are to be returned. This exception does not cover damage caused by later misuse, extend the thirty-day request period or establish an entitlement to a refund without assessment. Evidence and any required inspection remain applicable. Missing original packaging alone is not a sufficient reason to reject a qualifying damaged-item claim.

clauses.title: Grounds for a dispute
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.1 Grounds for a dispute
A dispute may be raised concerning: (a) a return parcel reported as not received; (b) missing goods, quantities, accessories or bundle components; (c) a different item in the returned parcel; (d) damage, a fault or a condition inconsistent with the accepted return reason; (e) the authenticity of purchased or returned goods; or (f) whether a change-of-mind return meets the applicable condition requirements. A dispute initiates a review. It does not establish that either party's account is correct or create a second refund entitlement.

clauses.section_title: Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
clauses.title: Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.2 Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
The original return reason, purchase details, supporting evidence and inspection findings will be considered together. Review must distinguish the original reported fault from an allegation of additional damage, missing contents or a different item during the return. The customer is not automatically responsible for damage merely because the goods were returned damaged. A qualifying original fault remains subject to section 2.5. Conflicting accounts or inspection findings will be referred for human review rather than automatic refund or rejection.

clauses.title: Counterfeit products
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.3 Counterfeit products
A claim concerning authenticity will be referred for human review. Relevant product, packaging and purchase evidence may be requested. A brand name, low price, image or allegation alone does not establish that goods are genuine or counterfeit. Any accepted resolution will identify the affected goods, whether physical return is required and the applicable refund. No special compensation or determination of authenticity is implied merely by raising the claim.

clauses.section_title: Goods returned due to change of mind
clauses.title: Goods returned due to change of mind
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.4 Goods returned due to change of mind
A dispute may arise where inspection reports use, missing original packaging or tags, missing accessories, an incomplete bundle or a different item. The applicable conditions are those in section 2.4 and the agreed return authorization. If the customer contests the finding, the request will be referred for human review. Where the original reason concerns arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item, section 2.5 must be considered rather than applying change-of-mind conditions without that exception.

clauses.title: Review and communication
clauses.text:

6.1 Conditions for payment
A refund is issued after the request has been accepted and, where a physical return is required, the returned goods have been received and the applicable inspection completed. The inspection considers the identity, quantities, completeness and conditions relevant to the original return reason, including any exception in section 2.5. A delay or a disputed finding may be raised for review under section 7. A return recorded as requested or received may still be progressing through the ordinary return process. clauses.title: Refund approval requirements
clauses.text:

6.6 Refund approval requirements

In particular, disputed findings, unavailable or unsafe evidence and unapproved exceptions must not be resolved by automatic payment. ## 6. Refunds

### REF-Refunds-6.1 Conditions for payment

A refund is issued after the request has been accepted and, where a physical return is required, the returned goods have been received and the applicable inspection completed. The inspection considers the identity, quantities, completeness and conditions relevant to the original return reason, including any exception in section 2.5. The store targets inspection within three (3) business days after warehouse receipt. Return tracking marked delivered does not itself establish that inspection is complete. A delay or a disputed finding may be raised for review under section 7. A return recorded as requested or received may still be progressing through the ordinary return process. That status alone does not require human review or establish that a refund is due. Routine progress enquiries may be answered automatically using the confirmed records. A disputed finding, unavailable required evidence or a request for human assistance must be referred for human review. Physical return may be waived following human review where non-delivery is confirmed or return is unsafe or impractical. The waiver applies only to the goods and resolution specified. It does not remove the requirement to establish the payment and refundable amount.

Related clauses: RET-ReturnEligibility-2.5, RET-ReturnParcelDisputes-7.1, RET-ReturnParcelDisputes-7.2, RET-ReturnParcelDisputes-7.3, RET-ReturnParcelDisputes-7.4, RET-ReturnParcelDisputes-7.5.

### REF-Refunds-6.2 Refund amount

The amount is based on the approved affected quantities and the amount paid for those goods, including the applicable recorded discount and tax allocations. It is not calculated using a later catalog price. Shipping components for returns are governed by section 5 of this Policy. For an accepted full cancellation before fulfillment, the recorded original shipping and tax are included, subject to the captured balance and earlier refunds. A partial return does not entitle the customer to reimbursement of retained or unaffected goods. Where the value of an accessory, a discount allocation or another component cannot be established, the amount requires review rather than an assumed allocation.

Related clauses: RET-ShippingFees-5.1, RET-ShippingFees-5.2.

### REF-Refunds-6.3 Payment destination and previous refunds

Refunds are made in SGD to the original payment method. They cannot be redirected to a different account or payment instrument supplied during a support conversation. The total of completed and pending refunds must not exceed the amount captured for the order. Amounts already refunded or reserved for an existing refund will be deducted from the remaining balance. Failed payments and uncaptured authorizations cannot be refunded as settled payments. Approval of a return does not authorize a duplicate refund.

### REF-Refunds-6.4 Refund timeframe

The store targets refund initiation within two (2) business days after final acceptance and completion of the required receipt and inspection, or an approved waiver. Return authorization alone does not start this period. After processing, supported card and PayNow refunds normally appear within five (5) to ten (10) business days. These are estimated periods rather than guaranteed posting dates. Requested, accepted and pending refunds may not yet have been processed.

### REF-Refunds-6.5 Delayed refunds and other resolutions

Where the relevant period has passed or the recorded status conflicts with the payment received, the customer may request further review. An additional refund will not be issued solely because an earlier refund is not yet visible. Exchange, replacement, repair, store credit and goodwill compensation require separate agreement. A request for one of these alternatives does not guarantee stock, dispatch or payment.

### REF-Refunds-6.6 Refund approval requirements

The approval requirements below apply only after the acceptance, inspection and payment conditions in sections 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 have been satisfied: (a) an eligible refund of SGD 30.00 or less may be processed automatically; (b) an eligible refund above SGD 30.00 and up to SGD 100.00 requires automated review before payment is approved; and (c) a refund above SGD 100.00 requires human review before payment is approved. Automated review must establish that the proposed action is supported by verified case facts, the applicable policy clauses and the approved refundable amount. A proposal that cannot be substantiated must be corrected or referred for human review; the amount alone does not establish eligibility. A requirement for human review elsewhere in this Policy takes precedence regardless of amount. In particular, disputed findings, unavailable or unsafe evidence and unapproved exceptions must not be resolved by automatic payment. An automatically issued return authorization does not establish that these payment requirements have been satisfied. The approval limits do not increase the captured balance available for refund, permit duplicate payment or allow a different payment destination.

Related clauses: REF-Refunds-6.1, REF-Refunds-6.2, REF-Refunds-6.3.

Returns and Refunds Policy
2.5 Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
Goods marked final sale at the time of purchase are excluded from change-of-mind returns. A product's general category or a label added after purchase does not establish that it was sold as final sale. Notwithstanding that exclusion, a request concerning verified arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item may be accepted within the period in section 2.1. In those circumstances, the unused and original-packaging conditions may be waived where opening, testing or loss of packaging was reasonably connected with discovering or reporting the fault. Secure return packaging is still required where the goods are to be returned. This exception does not cover damage caused by later misuse, extend the thirty-day request period or establish an entitlement to a refund without assessment. clauses.title: Conditions for payment
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.1 Conditions for payment
A refund is issued after the request has been accepted and, where a physical return is required, the returned goods have been received and the applicable inspection completed. The inspection considers the identity, quantities, completeness and conditions relevant to the original return reason, including any exception in section 2.5. The store targets inspection within three (3) business days after warehouse receipt. Return tracking marked delivered does not itself establish that inspection is complete. A delay or a disputed finding may be raised for review under section 7. A return recorded as requested or received may still be progressing through the ordinary return process. That status alone does not require human review or establish that a refund is due. Routine progress enquiries may be answered automatically using the confirmed records. A disputed finding, unavailable required evidence or a request for human assistance must be referred for human review. Physical return may be waived following human review where non-delivery is confirmed or return is unsafe or impractical. The waiver applies only to the goods and resolution specified. It does not remove the requirement to establish the payment and refundable amount.

clauses.title: Refund approval requirements
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.6 Refund approval requirements
The approval requirements below apply only after the acceptance, inspection and payment conditions in sections 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 have been satisfied: (a) an eligible refund of SGD 30.00 or less may be processed automatically; (b) an eligible refund above SGD 30.00 and up to SGD 100.00 requires automated review before payment is approved; and (c) a refund above SGD 100.00 requires human review before payment is approved. Automated review must establish that the proposed action is supported by verified case facts, the applicable policy clauses and the approved refundable amount. A proposal that cannot be substantiated must be corrected or referred for human review; the amount alone does not establish eligibility. A requirement for human review elsewhere in this Policy takes precedence regardless of amount. In particular, disputed findings, unavailable or unsafe evidence and unapproved exceptions must not be resolved by automatic payment. An automatically issued return authorization does not establish that these payment requirements have been satisfied. The approval limits do not increase the captured balance available for refund, permit duplicate payment or allow a different payment destination.

clauses.title: Refund timeframe
clauses.text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
6.4 Refund timeframe
The store targets refund initiation within two (2) business days after final acceptance and completion of the required receipt and inspection, or an approved waiver. Return authorization alone does not start this period. After processing, supported card and PayNow refunds normally appear within five (5) to ten (10) business days. These are estimated periods rather than guaranteed posting dates. Requested, accepted and pending refunds may not yet have been processed.

6.3 Payment destination and previous refunds
